findings.current: Silence hung over the fast ships as they cut rapidly through the current.
findings.defect: The draft changes the immediate setting from the single fast ship carrying the narrator to all four ships.
findings.rationale: The source uses the singular 쾌조선에는; the fleet of four is introduced separately afterward.
findings.replacement: Silence hung over the fast ship as it cut rapidly through the current.
findings.source: 빠르게 물살을 가르며 나아가는 쾌조선에는 침묵만이 감돌았다.

findings.current: Disciples from the two prestigious sects dividing Hubei Province filled the four fast ships.
findings.defect: Calling both powers sects misclassifies the Zhuge Clan.
findings.rationale: The two powers are the Zhuge Clan and Wudang; 대파 functions broadly here and does not make the Zhuge Clan a sect.
findings.replacement: Disciples from the two prestigious great factions that divided Hubei Province filled the four fast ships.
findings.source: 호북성을 양분하는 두 명문 대파의 제자들이 네 척의 쾌조선을 가득 채웠다.

findings.current: His position within Wudang and his standing in Murim were in no way inferior to Zhuge Feng’s.
findings.defect: The generic word “standing” loses the explicit Murim generational seniority expressed by 배분.
findings.rationale: 배분 denotes rank by martial lineage and generation, which explains why Zhuge Feng treats Hyeongong as a senior.
findings.replacement: His position within Wudang and his generational seniority in Murim were in no way inferior to Zhuge Feng’s.
findings.source: 그리고 그가 무당파 내에서 차지하는 위치나 무림의 배분은 결코 제갈풍에 뒤떨어지지 않았다.

findings.current: At Jeok Cheongang’s words, I muttered in disbelief.
findings.defect: The draft omits the narrator’s comic characterization of Jeok Cheongang as Murim’s Bodhidharma and an ancient veteran.
findings.rationale: The omitted appositive preserves both the Bodhidharma reference and the 고인물 joke about Jeok Cheongang’s extreme age and experience.
findings.replacement: At the words of Jeok Cheongang—Murim’s own Bodhidharma and the ultimate old-timer—I muttered in disbelief.
findings.source: 무림의 달마대사 고인물, 적천강의 말에 어이가 없어진 내가 중얼거렸다.

findings.current:
“Since we’re on the subject, how old are you, exactly?”

“Old?”

Jeok Cheongang usually took any mention of his age as synonymous with asking someone to kill him. I awkwardly changed the word.

“…Then, how many years have you lived?”

“How many years?”
findings.defect: The first question directly calls him old, while the source uses one highly respectful term for age and then switches to another; the narration also broadens his reaction from being called old to any mention of age.
findings.rationale: 춘추 and 연세 are both deferential age terms. Preserving Taekyung’s escalating politeness is necessary for the punchline when he finally addresses Jeok Cheongang like a child.
findings.replacement:
“Since we’re on the subject, may I ask your venerable age?”

“My venerable age?”

Even under ordinary circumstances, Jeok Cheongang treated being called old as synonymous with asking him to kill you. I awkwardly tried another term.

“…Then, how many years have you lived, sir?”

“How many years?”
findings.source:
“이렇게 된 김에 여쭤보는 건데, 춘추가 정확히 얼마나 되시는 겁니까?”

“춘추?”

평소에도 늙었다는 소리를 죽여 달라는 것과 동의어로 받아들이는 적천강이다. 나는 떨떠름하게 단어를 고쳤다.

“……그럼, 연세?”

“연세?”

findings.current: And beyond it, a violent whirlpool twisting like a blade.
findings.defect: The draft reverses the whirlpool’s spatial relationship to the narrow passage.
findings.rationale: 그 앞에서 places the whirlpool in front of the narrow stretch, not beyond it.
findings.replacement: And directly in front of it, a violent whirlpool twisting like a blade.
findings.source: 그리고 그 앞에서 칼날처럼 회오리치는 거센 와류(渦流)가.

findings.current: “We have not heard from him in a long time. Let us consider him dead.”
findings.defect: The draft omits 다시, losing the continuity detail that contact with their father was restored and then lost again.
findings.rationale: 다시 explicitly marks a renewed loss of contact rather than one uninterrupted absence.
findings.replacement: “We lost contact with him again a long time ago. Let us consider him dead.”
findings.source: “다시 소식이 끊긴 지 오래됐다. 그냥 죽은 셈 치자꾸나.”

findings.current: And while he was at it, he had even killed off his father, who was alive and well because he had dumped his family duties and run away.
findings.defect: The syntax makes abandoning the family duties the reason their father is alive and well, rather than the reason Jin Wikyung declares his living father dead.
findings.rationale: The source’s causal link is that Jin Wikyung writes his father off because he fled after foisting the family duties on him.
findings.replacement: And while he was at it, he had declared our perfectly alive father dead just because the man had dumped the family responsibilities on him and run away.
findings.source: 그 와중에 가문 짬 때리고 도망쳤다고 멀쩡히 살아 있는 아버지까지 죽여 버리는 클라스.

findings.defect: Taekyung is confirming that Mu Song’s claim is true, not commenting on Mu Song’s sincerity or demeanor.
findings.rationale: 진짜네 is a realization that it truly is too late to stop, directly validating the preceding statement.

findings.current:
He was right.

Violently, fucking right.
findings.defect: The second sentence is unnatural English and does not convey the wordplay between 맞는 meaning “correct” and 처맞는 meaning “getting beaten.”
findings.rationale: The replacement preserves the abrupt repetition and converts the Korean homonym joke into natural English without changing Taekyung’s hostility.
findings.replacement:
He had a point.

A fucking punchable one.

summary: Actionable fidelity issues include altered scope and spatial relations, lost hierarchy and register, an omitted characterization joke, and changed causal and continuity details.
